topic: You don't have to do a local recon here - you can search your context for all the relevant stuff that you need (and perhaps even read in some of the solutoins and plans). I want to learn more about production software architecture here. I don't personally like the shape of how the current repo is structured (domain/services/etc) - fine that it works, but I want to be able to reference something authoritative here. And since we're deeper into compute land, I'm sure that things are going to be idiosyncratic (i.e., i'm sure mvvm works great when you have microservices and a CRUD app - or wahtever), but I want to know where I can dig deeper into how to actually think about this. I have some general thoughts on the way that I would want this framed, in terms of the way that th edata is shaped, how that gets passed around, the objects/structs that i would be operating on, but i don't know if i have a good external grounding of the types of resources that are available for that kind of work. Does that make sense? I really just want to have a decent grasp on this. you can help me refine the research angles

angles.brief: Round-2 brief for Angle 01 (Literature Map): (1) Produce a per-source fetch-evidence log for the ten read-first sources — URL fetched vs publisher page only; the synthesis' 'all sources verified by angle 01 unless noted' overstates coverage. (2) Resolve the Cockburn hexagon URL dispute: angle 01 claims live verification of https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture while angle 07 reports fetch failure — re-fetch, pin URL variant + status + timestamp, record evidence. (3) Resolve Simon 1962 'The Architecture of Complexity' JSTOR stable ID https://www.jstor.org/stable/985870 or replace with the APS 106(6) citation — the nearly-decomposable-hierarchy claim rests on it. (4) Re-anchor the central mapping (repo seams = hexagon ports, headless coordinator = driver adapter): the class mapped, OptimizeCoordinator, is consumed only by test/lifecycle/coordinator_test.cpp; production wiring is MainScreen → OptimizerRunController → OptimizerManagerRunDriver (fresh manager + QThread per run, optimizer_run_controller.cpp:127/:144; plan 006 U5) — name the production class and its real ports. (5) Locate the exact ITK-chapter passage for 'registration does not stream' and note the extrapolation to GPU residency is the angle's own leap. (6) Check DDIA 2nd-edition announcement (2026) before it stays in the pathway. NON-OVERLAP: do not re-map sources or re-survey the canon; only the fetch-evidence log, the two URL resolutions, and the production re-anchor.

Round-2 brief for Angle 02 (MVVM Critique): (1) Re-anchor the worker-thread claims: production uses OptimizerRunController + OptimizerManagerRunDriver — fresh driver per run (M12/Q8, optimizer_run_controller.cpp:127), fresh manager + QThread per run (optimizer_run_driver.cpp:28-33), H3 bounded-wait destructor contract (never delete a running thread, :36-49); OptimizeCoordinator (persistent worker) is exercised only by test/lifecycle/coordinator_test.cpp. The queued-signal advice still holds; the 'persistent worker' premise is wrong for production. (2) Reconcile the segfault narrative: U4 convention (docs/solutions/conventions/jtml-testability-and-cmake-conventions-2026-08-07.md §5) documents per-run threads causing the dangling-pointer destructor segfault, but plan 006 (2026-08-11) deliberately reintroduced per-run threads with the H3 contract as the actual fix — state the current production truth. (3) Audit SettingsBridge.cpp (src/app/experimental/, 78 matches) against the ViewModel-bloat trajectory: what does it actually bind (properties, count, frequency)? (4) Check whether any per-eval signal exists today (optimizer_manager.cpp:1198-1203 UpdateDisplay cadence) and size the PM-for-form-state fit. (5) Verify whether the arXiv MLR (2504.18191) evidence is Qt/QML-specific or WPF/mobile-only. (6) Look for Qt6-doc/KDAB statements quantifying binding overhead. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the MVVM failure-mode inventory; only re-anchor the worker claims + audit the VM layer scope.

Round-2 brief for Angle 03 (Data-Centric Design): (1) QUANTIFY the real JTML boundary flow: sum per-eval cudaMemcpy sizes across render_engine.cu:781-790 (render bbox 4×int + fragment_fill 1×int), fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289-290 (FIDM pixel_score 1×int), distance_map_metric.cu:117-126 (distance_map_score + edge_pixels_count 2×int) — ~32 bytes total per monoplane eval. The 'transfer budget'/data-movement-dominates framing (echoed in synthesis recommended course step 3) outruns the evidence; the correct frame is sync LATENCY/pipeline drain (handoff-2026-08-12 §4 '≥95%-host-block'), not bytes. State which of the 5 copies are individually necessary (e.g. could bbox stay device-side for FIDM?). (2) Characterize the actual DIRECT storage: direct_data_storage.cpp:19-43,93-121 is vector<vector<HyperBox6D*>> — sorted columns of heap pointers + parallel minimum_value_columns_/size_columns_ vectors; the 'already structurally SoA' claim (angle 07 C3) is wrong — it is pointer-chasing AoS with per-insert new; count new sites per DIRECT iteration. (3) Resolve the keep-and-justify vs data-shaped tension with the repo facts: would a data-shaped re-decomposition move files or only change internals/contracts? (4) Answer whether the stage-graph container/executor runs in production (StageScript types ARE consumed by Optimize() since U9 — optimizer_stage_script.h:12; the executor/selection is not — plan 009). (5) Re-base C-family options on the measured ~7k evals/s (handoff §4, ≈143 μs/eval wall, RTX 3090 Ti) — which C-options survive. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the DOD/DOP/style taxonomy; only the quantified boundary flow + actual storage layout.

Round-2 brief for Angle 04 (Language Affordances): (1) Count the domain lib's translation units: src/domain/CMakeLists.txt:12-24 lists 10 .cpp files (ambiguous_pose_processing, data_structures_6D, direct_data_storage, direct_optimizer, model_list_builder, optimize_intent_controller, pose_copy, pose_file_io, session_state, sym_trap_functions) — the '9 pure files' (angles 04/07 D2) is uncounted; locate the purity-gate enforcement (CMakeLists.txt:4-7 documents it as a comment only — convention, not CI; verify if any script/CI label exists). (2) Inventory the actual cxx interop surface: which types/functions in include/domain/*.h would cross a cxx seam (Pose6D? DirectOptimizer? StageScript?) and what each requires at the boundary. (3) Decide what problem Rust adoption is solving against the repo's actual failure history: the one documented GPU corruption (.panoptes/optimizer-deep-dive) was a wrong index formula at distance_map_metric.cu:27 — an index-logic bug, not a memory-safety defect; Rust cannot reach the buffer-ownership problem across a C-ABI seam (CostFunctionManager holds raw pointers to GPU frame vectors; UploadData takes pointer-to-vector-of-pointers, CostFunctionManager.cpp:100-134). (4) Note the SIMT/coalescing lever is latent: repo evaluates single poses sequentially (costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION per eval, biplane OFF — CostFunctionManager.cpp:95), no batching exists. (5) Re-check rust-cuda/cuda-oxide against the pinned CUDA 12.4 toolchain (pixi.toml:7,13-14,40-49) — version compatibility, not just activity. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the feature/consequence survey or FFI doctrine; only the seam inventory + problem definition.

Round-2 brief for Angle 05 (Stack-Native Guidance): (1) Re-anchor the worker pattern: production wires MainScreen → OptimizerRunController (mainscreen.cpp:181-206) → OptimizerManagerRunDriver — fresh driver per run (optimizer_run_controller.cpp:127 ':144 driver_ = factory_()'), fresh manager + QThread per run, H3 bounded-wait destructor contract (optimizer_run_driver.cpp:36-49: cooperative stop, bounded wait, never delete a running thread). OptimizeCoordinator + OptimizeWorker + moveToThread is TEST-ONLY. Evaluate: is the U5/H3 shape itself the Qt-stack-native pattern (deleteLater chain, bounded wait) satisfying thread-affinity rules? (2) Resolve the 7k evals/s question definitively: docs/handoff-2026-08-12-optimizer-path.md §4 records ~7,000 evals/s measured on RTX 3090 Ti over the whole multistage run (~15 s) — a wall-clock count, so per-eval syncs are included by construction; per-eval wall ≈143 μs. The angles treated this as open; it is answered in-repo. (3) Re-fetch + pin the disputed URLs: NVIDIA 'How to Overlap Data Transfers' blog (angle 05 verified live, angle 07 404'd) and Cockburn hexagon (angle 01 verified, angle 07 failed); pin CUDA 12.4 archived docs (docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.4.x/...). (4) Check whether any non-default stream exists in src/compute (are all 5 D2H copies on the default stream?). (5) Re-derive CUDA Graphs upside on measured numbers: at ≈143 μs/eval wall, NVIDIA's 9.6→3.4 μs launch-overhead microbenchmark is ~7% of per-eval time — restate 'the single most stack-native optimization' on the real baseline. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the Qt/VTK/CUDA guidance survey; only the production re-anchor + URL pins + baseline re-derivation.

Round-2 brief for Angle 06 (Case Studies): (1) Re-anchor Pattern 5 (compute walled from UI) and the Slicer progress/abort lesson to the production class: fresh-thread-per-run OptimizerManagerRunDriver + H3 contract (plan 006 U5; optimizer_run_driver.cpp:28-33,36-49), NOT the test-only OptimizeCoordinator persistent worker. (2) Answer whether MTime-style invalidation can skip real work in JTML's eval loop: costFunctionDIRECT_DILATION (DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:58-103) → gpu_model.cu:115-124 → render_engine.cu Render re-renders every eval with no caching — what per-eval stage outputs, if any, persist between evals? The 're-execute only dirty stages' advice may have zero applicable work to skip. (3) Pin the disputed Slicer URLs (angle 07 reported developer-architecture 404s; angle 06 fetched MRML/module pages OK) and the GHOST toolkit attribution (DeepWiki-derived, medium confidence) — resolve with evidence. (4) Verify MITK micro-service registry currency (2016.11 docs cited) vs CostFunctionManager register-by-interface (7 variants). (5) Verify OptimizerRunLaunch immutability: defined where, passed BY VALUE (optimizer_run_controller.cpp:147), no mutation in driver? (6) Scope the 'no MVVM/no QML at core' negative claim to the actually-fetched subset. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the four case-study surveys; only the URL pins + the invalidation-applicability question (repo side owned by brief 3).

Round-2 brief for Angle 07 (JTML Re-Framing): (1) RE-MEASURE and re-state every option's premises on the real numbers: mainscreen.cpp = 5,045 lines (not ~5,115, E1); optimizer_manager.cpp = 1,538 lines (not ~1,700, B1/C4/D1); domain = 10 pure .cpp files (not 9, D2 — src/domain/CMakeLists.txt:12-24); kernels ≈12-13 per monoplane eval (render ≈5 + 2 CUB DeviceScan launches at render_engine.cu:313/:764 + FIDM 4 + DM 2), biplane ≈20. (2) Re-anchor EVERY option that names the coordinator: production orchestrator is OptimizerRunController (pure core: core_.onRunStarted, epochs) + OptimizerManagerRunDriver; OptimizeCoordinator (headless state machine) is test-only. A1/B1/B2/D1/C7 target a class production doesn't run — restate what changes if re-pointed to the production classes. (3) Correct the stage-surface claim: production Optimize() CONSUMES BuildStageScript/StageScript (optimizer_stage_script.h:12, optimizer_manager.h:301) since plan 008 U7/U9; what is unconsumed is the stage-graph executor/selection (plan 009) — re-base C4's 'highest R15 risk' framing on what is actually consumed. (4) Re-derive C5's upside: at measured ~7k evals/s (≈143 μs/eval wall, handoff §4 — which explicitly refutes the prior run's derived 20–60), NVIDIA's 9.6→3.4 μs launch-overhead figure is ~7% of per-eval time — the launch-overhead tax premise needs re-derivation; state which C-options survive the measured baseline. (5) Correct the injected-cost signature: std::function<double(const Point6D&)> (direct_optimizer.h:28), not std::function<double(const double*)>. (6) Correct the C3 SoA claim: direct_data_storage.cpp:19-43,93-121 is vector<vector<HyperBox6D*>> — pointer-chasing AoS with per-insert new, not SoA. (7) Reconcile the struct sketch with repo reality: which sketch structs exist (OptimizerRunLaunch, StageSpec/StageScript in src/coordinator) and which are new (Pose6D, EvalRequest/EvalResult, CostSample, StateEvent) — and where the crossing table implies they live. (8) Verify the ms/call meter claim (optimizer_manager.cpp:1199 clock()/cost_function_calls_) and whether the C7 honest-meter fix touches optimizer_manager.cpp or mainscreen.cpp. NON-OVERLAP: do not redo the 19-option menu or struct sketch; only re-anchor to corrected numbers, production classes, and consumed-vs-unconsumed stage surface.

planSummary: 7 layers, all thinking=high. Run name: compute-app-architecture-grounding. TWO ROUNDS pre-authorized: round 1 = 7 parallel librarians; round 2 = deepen pass on ALL angles (gap-review briefs must name concrete gaps per angle). Angle 7 (JTML re-framing) output must be a WIDE menu of divergent re-framing options — no prescription, offered for user consideration. Top-level synthesis MUST include a section presenting a menu of options to consider (not a single recommendation). Personas: 01-authoritative-literature-map = panoptes-librarian-docs (curated); 02-mvvm-critique, 03-data-centric-design, 04-language-affordances, 05-stack-native-guidance, 06-case-studies, 07-jtml-reframing = generated role blocks embedded against panoptes-librarian-generic. LOCAL CONTEXT from context-sourced recon (local-recon.org): Qt6 6.7.2 + VTK 9.3 + CUDA 12.4 + OpenCV C++20, DIRECT global optimizer over GPU cost; current domain/services/coordinator/compute/view/app layering derived from testability seams, NEVER external literature (plan 003 External References empty); R15 behavior preservation + R12 no premature abstraction are normative; seams: OptimizeCoordinator, DirectOptimizer injected cost, CostFunctionManager (7 variants), stage-graph registry, SettingsBridge VM, pose_file_io; jtml_domain is planned Rust-interop surface.
